page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. No marginal notes. Running head at the top, page number beside it. Catchword "non" at the lower right, below the last full line.

main_text.p: prætermissa sunt, vel ea detrahere, quæ à nonnullis non solùm inutilia, sed & maxi-me noxia reperiuntur. Huiusmodi autem sunt, quæ ad doloris sedationem extrinse-cus ab his admoueri solent, ut astringetia[?], plurimùm relaxantia, & immoderatè refri-gerantia. Quæ in primis astringunt, sedem affectam comprimendo, dolores intenduntur, fluxionesq; maiores cient. Deinde materi-am, quæ articulis parit dolorem constrin-gendo, resolui prohibent: proinde illa par-ti affectæ magis ac magis impingunt. Præ-staret ergo hæc supra ponere ad sistendam fluxionem: sic enim nullam noxam inferre possent, modò ante corpus ritè expurgatum sit. Quæ præterea plurimùm laxant super-posita morbum insanabilem reddunt, pro-pterea articulorum imbecillitatem inten-dunt. Quòd sanè euenisse Geneuæ mercatori cuidem Lugdunæo, cui Prunardus nomen erat, certò scimus. Huiusmodi autem quæ à recentioribus scribuntur, sunt unguentum resumptiuum, stillatitia canicu-lorum aqua, rapæ in lacte percoctæ, medulla calsiæ fistulæ in aqua violarum dis-soluta. Quæ insuper stupefaciendi uim habent, siue intus assumpta, siue foris admota

page.notes: Doubtful readings: "astringetia" (the printed form may be "astringentia"); "calsiæ" as printed, possibly "calamiæ" or a misprint. The text ends at "admota"; "non" is the catchword. Long s normalised to plain s throughout. "eueniffe" written as "euenisse" per the long-s rule. Not checked against an edition.
